kinds.@image: the kind of a file (a photo or picture): shown beside its size in the Files view, as its Kind in the file's details, and under its name in search and @-mentions
kinds.@pdf: the kind of a file: a PDF document (shown like the other kinds in this group)
kinds.@document: the kind of a file: a word-processor document (.docx, .odt, .pages)
kinds.@spreadsheet: the kind of a file: a spreadsheet (.xlsx, .csv, .numbers)
kinds.@presentation: the kind of a file: slides (.pptx, .key)
kinds.@audio: the kind of a file: a sound recording or music
kinds.@video: the kind of a file: a video
kinds.@archive: the kind of a file: a compressed archive (.zip, .rar)
kinds.@code: the kind of a file: source code (.js, .py, .html)
kinds.@text: the kind of a file: plain text (.txt, .md)
kinds.@file: the kind of a file that is none of the other kinds: just a file

files.@subtitle: under the Files view's title: how many files the library has and their total size; {size} is a size like 3.2 MB
files.emptySubtitle: Everything you attach and drop in, in one place
files.@addFiles: button that opens the system's file picker to add files to the library
files.@layout: screen-reader name of the switch between showing files as a grid or a list
files.@grid: option that shows files as a grid of tiles (a tooltip on its icon)
files.@list: option that shows files as a list of rows (a tooltip on its icon)
files.@kindFilter: screen-reader name of the row of chips that filter the Files view by kind of file

filter.@all: filter chip that shows every file
filter.@images: filter chip that shows only pictures
filter.@documents: filter chip that shows only documents (PDFs, word-processor files, spreadsheets, slides, text)
filter.@media: filter chip that shows only audio and video files
filter.@otherKinds: filter chip that shows the files of other kinds (archives, code, anything else)
filter.@unused: filter chip that shows the files no page or assignment uses

files.@sortBy: heading of the menu that chooses the order of files

sort.@dateAdded: order of files: newest added first (a menu item, and the sort button's label)
sort.name: Name
sort.@name: order of files: by their names, A to Z (a menu item, and the sort button's label)
sort.@size: order of files: largest first (a menu item, and the sort button's label)

files.@search: placeholder of the box that finds files by name in the Files view
files.@missing: shown instead of a file's size when the file is gone from the disk (a state, not a command)
files.@usedInPlaces: tooltip on a file tile's link icon: how many pages and assignments use the file
files.@uses: a narrow column in the list of files: how many pages and assignments use the file, or that none do
files.emptyText: Drop files here, attach them to assignments, or drag them into a page. They’re kept on this computer.
files.@dropToAdd: shown while files are dragged over the Files view; Files is the view's name
files.@addedFile: message after one file was added to the library; {name} is the file's name
files.@addedFiles: message after several files were added to the library at once
files.@tooLarge: message when a file is too big to add; {name} is the file's name, {limit} the largest size allowed, like 250 MB

trashInUse.one: “{name}” is used in {count} place. It keeps working there until you empty the Trash.
trashInUse.other: “{name}” is used in {count} places. It keeps working there until you empty the Trash.

files.@trashInUse: asks before moving a file that pages or assignments use to the Trash; {name} is the file's name, {count} how many places use it
files.@movedToTrash: message after a file was moved to the Trash; {name} is the file's name
files.@savedToDownloads: message after a copy of a file was saved; {name} is the copy's file name, Downloads the computer's downloads folder

preview.label: File preview
preview.missing: This file is missing from the Thought Desk folder.
preview.@missing: in the file preview when the file is gone from the disk; Thought Desk is the app's name, the folder where it keeps its files
preview.noPreview: No preview for this kind of file.
preview.@details: heading above a file's kind, size, date added and tags
preview.@kind: label of the row that says what kind of file it is (Image, PDF…)
preview.@size: label of the row with the file's size
preview.@added: label of the row with when the file was added ("3 days ago")
preview.@usedIn: heading above the list of pages and assignments that use the file
preview.notUsed: Not used in any page or assignment
preview.gone: This file is no longer in your library.

flashcards.emptySubtitle: Make cards in any page, then study them here
flashcards.@dueToday: start of the line under the Flashcards view's title: how many cards are waiting today, or that none are; followed by " · " and the count of cards and decks
flashcards.@cardsInDeck: end of the line under the Flashcards view's title when all cards are in one deck; {count} is the number of cards (it picks the form), {decks} is 1
flashcards.@cardsInDecks: end of the line under the Flashcards view's title when there are several decks; {count} is the number of cards (it picks the form), {decks} the number of decks
flashcards.@study: button that starts studying, with how many cards are waiting (just Study when none are)
flashcards.@allDecks: title of a study session with the cards from every deck
flashcards.@decks: heading above the list of flashcard decks (pages with flashcards) when no course has any
flashcards.@otherDecks: heading above the decks that aren't in any course's notes, below the courses' decks
flashcards.emptyText: Type /flashcard in any page. Write the front, press Enter for the back, and Enter again for the next card.
flashcards.@emptyText: /flashcard is the command typed in a page to make a card: keep it as written (or write the Flashcard block's name in your language after the slash); Enter is the key
flashcards.@cardCount: how many flashcards a deck has
flashcards.@due: how many of a deck's cards are due for review today
flashcards.@new: how many of a deck's cards haven't been studied yet
flashcards.@mastered: how much of a deck has been learned well; {percent} is a whole number from 0 to 100
flashcards.noCards: No flashcards yet. Type /flashcard in a page.
flashcards.@noCards: /flashcard is the command typed in a page to make a card: keep it as written (or write the Flashcard block's name in your language after the slash)
flashcards.resetMessage: Every card in “{title}” will be new again.
flashcards.@resetMessage: asks before forgetting what was learned of a deck; {title} is the deck's page title
flashcards.@reset: button that confirms forgetting a deck's progress

study.label: Study {title}
study.@label: screen-reader name of the study window; {title} is what is being studied (a deck's page, a course, or All Decks)
study.@shuffle: tooltip of the button that shows the cards in random order (it is off)
study.@shuffled: tooltip of the same button while the cards are in random order (it is on)
study.@answerFirst: tooltip of the button that swaps a card's sides, so you're shown the answer and recall the question (it is off)
study.@answerFirstOn: tooltip of the same button while the sides are swapped (it is on)
study.@progress: how far a study session is; {learned} is the number of cards done, {total} the number in the session
study.@review: above a card's question: a card studied before, coming back for review
study.@new: above a card's question: a card never studied before
study.@reviewAnswerFirst: above a card's question: a card studied before, with its sides swapped (Answer first is on)
study.@newAnswerFirst: above a card's question: a card never studied before, with its sides swapped (Answer first is on)
study.@summary: at the end of a study session: how many cards, how many were remembered the first time ({percent}, a whole number), and how long it took ({duration}, like 4 min)
study.breakdown: How the cards went the first time
study.@neededAnotherLook: at the end of a study session: how many cards were answered Again (forgotten)
study.@moreDue: at the end of a study session: how many cards are still waiting today
study.@twoSentences: at the end of a study session, two whole sentences one after the other: {first} is how many cards needed another look, {second} how many are still due; put between them what your language puts between sentences (a space in English, nothing in Chinese or Japanese)
study.@seconds: how long a study session took, in seconds (short)
study.@minutes: how long a study session took, in minutes (short)
study.@hoursMinutes: how long a study session took, in hours and minutes (short); {hours} is a whole number of hours, {minutes} the minutes left over, 0 to 59
study.@undo: button that takes back the last answer given to a card
study.howWell: How well did you know it?
study.@spaceToShow: hint: pressing the Space bar turns the card over
study.@done: button that closes a finished study session

grades.@again: answer to a flashcard: forgotten, show it again soon (as in Anki)
grades.@hard: answer to a flashcard: remembered with difficulty (as in Anki)
grades.@good: answer to a flashcard: remembered (as in Anki)
grades.@easy: answer to a flashcard: remembered easily (as in Anki)

gaps.@now: under a flashcard answer button: the card comes back in this session
gaps.@days: under a flashcard answer button: when the card comes back
gaps.@weeks: under a flashcard answer button: when the card comes back, in weeks (short, the button is narrow)
gaps.@months: under a flashcard answer button: when the card comes back, in months (short, the button is narrow)
gaps.@years: under a flashcard answer button: when the card comes back, in years (short, the button is narrow); {count} can have a decimal, like 1.5

controls.@filter: placeholder of a box that narrows a list as you type
controls.@color: screen-reader name of a row of colour swatches
controls.@custom: screen-reader name of the swatch that holds a colour of your own
controls.@hueStrength: what a screen reader says for the colour wheel; {hue} is an angle from 0 to 360, {strength} a whole number from 0 to 100
